Interface BeanTypeHierarchy

All Known Implementing Classes:
GeneratedBeanTypeHierarchy
public interface BeanTypeHierarchy
The hierarchy of an introspected type, generated at compile time when the type is introspected with Introspected.hierarchy(): every super class and interface of the type, with the super class and the interfaces each of them declares, and the methods the type itself declares.

The types are those the compiler saw: the type itself first, then, depth first, its super class and the super classes and interfaces of that, then its interfaces and theirs, each once. Object is reported as a super class, it is not described itself.

The types are raw: the type arguments a type passes to its super class and interfaces are not described.

Each bean method of the introspection knows its declaring levels: the type declaring it and every type of the hierarchy declaring a method it overrides, whether or not that method is a bean method. A bean method the introspected type does not declare is inherited. The methods are looked up by identity: pass the BeanMethod instances of the introspection the hierarchy belongs to.

Only bean methods are described here. The declarations of a property, the field and the accessor of every type declaring one, are the members of the property, each reporting its declaring type, when the introspection is generated with Introspected.members(). A bean method has no such per-declaration element, so its declaring levels are listed here.

This interface is implemented by generated code only. Methods may be added to it in later versions without a default implementation.

Since:
5.3.0

    • getDeclaringTypes

      List<Class<?>> getDeclaringTypes(BeanMethod<?,?> method)
      The declaring levels of a bean method: the type declaring it, then every type of the hierarchy declaring a method it overrides, each once, nearest first: in the breadth first order of the hierarchy of the introspected type, the super class before the interfaces, so a type the introspected type extends or implements directly comes before a type that one extends or implements in turn. An inherited method overrides the methods of the interfaces the introspected type introduces as well, those are levels too. Class.isInterface() tells which levels are interfaces.
      Parameters:
      method - A bean method instance of the introspection, compared by identity
      Returns:
      The declaring types, empty for a method that is not a bean method of the introspection
